Name: reink_chart_robustness
Title: ReInk: OCR Re-Rendered Views for Robust Chart Question Answering under Visual Degradations
Short Hypothesis: For corrupted chart images, providing a VLM with an auxiliary re-inked OCR view (OCR text re-rendered as a separate image at detected locations) improves chart QA accuracy beyond a compute-matched blank second image and a scrambled-text control that preserves box layout but destroys text semantics.
Related Work: ChartQAPro (Masry et al., 2025) is a real-world chart QA benchmark with 1,948 questions where best closed model reaches 55.81% vs human 85.02%. CHART NOISe / Losing the Plot (Shin et al., 2025) shows sharp drops under blur: GPT-4o drops from 70% to 45% under major Gaussian blur. ViCrop (Zhang et al., 2023) uses attention-based cropping for small details. CropVLM (Carvalho et al., 2025) trains a crop-selection policy via RL. No prior work uses a spatially aligned OCR re-rendered canvas as an auxiliary image input for chart QA robustness.

benchmarks: ChartQAPro (1,948 questions, corrupted with defocus blur and pixelate at severity 4)
notes: PERFECTLY suited for Gemini API -- just send 2 images + question per call
Also works with local Qwen2.5-VL-7B on RTX 5080 (~14GB VRAM)
EasyOCR for text extraction runs on CPU
Canvas rendering with PIL is trivial
Success: C exceeds max(A-SC4, B) by >=2pp on corrupted set
